subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should `sessions_spawn` select only operator-configured sub-agent lanes under an aggregate concurrency cap, or should OpenClaw keep one fixed global lane?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but repository evidence cannot decide whether lane identity is trusted operator policy, an unrestricted model input, or better expressed through target-agent concurrency; that choice defines resource-exhaustion and compatibility behavior.

options.title: Configured bounded lanes
options.body: Add an optional lane selector that accepts only configured lane IDs, retains the existing default, and enforces both per-lane and aggregate sub-agent caps.

options.title: Target-agent limits only
options.body: Address isolation through per-agent concurrency such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8061, without introducing workload-class lane names.

options.title: Keep one global lane
options.body: Retain the current scalar scheduler and document separate gateways or agent profiles as the isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Configured bounded lanes
recommendation.body: Add an optional lane selector that accepts only configured lane IDs, retains the existing default, and enforces both per-lane and aggregate sub-agent caps.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature and concurrency history most strongly connects this person to the public scheduling contract that needs a durable direction.
